author: NASASpaceflight
description:
This Week In Spaceflight covers China’s successful first landing of an orbital-class booster on the debut flight of the Chang Zheng 10B rocket, Blue Origin’s ongoing work at Launch Complex 36 and fit-checks for the Blue Moon Endurance lander, Starship Flight 13 preparations including Booster 20 rollout and a record-length static fire at Pad 2, NASA beginning stacking of the Artemis III SLS in the Vehicle Assembly Building, and major contract wins and hardware progress from Europe’s Isar Aerospace, Rocket Factory Augsburg, MaiaSpace, and PLD Space. 

The episode also discusses ispace’s new lunar payload aggregation service for Starship landings, space debris from a foreign rocket washing ashore in Australia, Jeremy Hansen’s retirement from the Canadian Space Agency, Relativity Space and Impulse Space joining the U.S. Space Force’s NSSL Phase 3 program, Hayabusa2’s asteroid flyby, and SpaceX’s Transporter 17 mission.

title: China Lands Orbital-Class Booster for First Time - Historic Success | This Week in Spaceflight
